chapter_theme: Agasthiyar's first run of ஞானம்: the one God is the Self and Shakti within, known by a mind subdued through devotion and held at the inner whorl (சுழி), and such a knower is one in a crore. Around that centre the verses attack the four Vedas and their teachers as a livelihood path that leaves everyone wailing in the streets, ask where the breath goes at death and admit no one sees it, and close with a code of plain conduct: truth, no killing, no lying, no anger, no disputation.
structure_note: Nine எண்சீர் விருத்தம் stanzas addressed to 'my children' (என்மக்காள்) and 'அப்பா'. They chain by antadi, each opening with the last word of the one before (மோட்சம், பாரு, ஒருவன், மோட்சம், மூச்சு, பாரு, சத்தியம்). 2405 to 2409 set out the one God and the rarity of the knower; 2410 and 2411 turn to the breath's departure at death and what no one sees; 2412 widens to births in the cosmos and the body as cosmos; 2413 ends with rules of conduct.

2405.reading: Shakti, the Supreme, alone is God and has become the life of every living being; those who know this by intellect are the meritorious, one in a crore on earth; the supreme jnani, mind subdued by devotion, stands in the state and does not let the mind drift into the void, and knowing the state in the whorl is itself moksha.
2405.nuance: The sense turns on two coded words. பாழ் here is where the mind must not be let go, a negative emptiness, unlike the fertile void of Tirumular's usage. சுழி (whorl) is read by tradition as the suzhumunai, the central channel at the brow, so that 'knowing the state in the whorl' is a yogic instruction; a plain reading takes it as the still point in the turning mind. சுத்தியே யலைவதில்லை (does not wander in circling) is unclear in syntax.

2406.reading: The secret for gaining moksha is this: do not lie, steal or kill with deceit, throw out fever and anger, set your mind on merit in this world, do not leap or go to waste, and look again and again at the many Vedas and shastras, the path made so the blameless may live; think it over, my children.
2406.nuance: The verse is plainer than the rest of the run, and the line on the Vedas sits oddly beside 2407 and 2411, which say the Vedas are a livelihood and have come to nothing. பிழைக்கச் செய்த மார்க்கம் can mean 'the path made so they may be saved' or, as in 2407, 'the path made so they may make a living'; on the second reading the praise is ironic. காய்ச்சல் is literally fever, here perhaps heat of temper.

2407.reading: Look at the four Vedas, all four: are they for planting attachment and desire, or a pledge worth crores? Each contradicts the other; it is a path made in vain for their livelihood; they wail street by street, and not one of them sees the divine state; who is going to stand firm? the wonder is one in a crore.
2407.nuance: Line 3 ஒன்றொன்றுக்கு கொன்றை மாறி is corrupt; the sense wanted is ஒன்றுக்கொன்று மாறி, each at variance with the other. பிணையோ கோடி (a pledge of crores) may be a sneer at the price put on Vedic learning. அவர்பிழைக்க is here plainly 'for them to make a living', which colours the same phrase in 2406.

2408.reading: Worship God as one, live on the earth as a noble man, sow the crop in its season, and like the supreme jnani do not let the mind go to waste; thieves roam by crores upon crores, cheats fill the land by crores, and many crores will come and beguile you with words: they are thieves.
2408.nuance: The thieves are religious teachers, as 2410 (deceiving gurus) and the whole run make clear. பருவமதிற் சேறுபயிர் (sow the wet field in season) can be plain farming advice, as the verse's picture of an upright householder, or a figure for practice done at the right time.

2409.reading: The Self that is called 'I' and 'he' is itself the one God; worship always the Lord who, when father and mother joined, came holding the embryo as 'I'; even the thief called king knows this one in crores upon crores; one must know the 'why' by the mind, and standing firm, my children, is moksha.
2409.nuance: The God who 'came holding the embryo as I' is the self that enters at conception, so that the one God is the inner self rather than any external deity; this is the plainest statement of the run's theology. கோனென்ற திருடனுக்குந் தெரியும் is odd: either even the thief-king knows, or the thief who calls himself king (the false guru) knows of the rare one. ஏனென்றே அறிய வேணும், 'one must know why', is unusual and may mean knowing the cause.

2410.reading: Hear the secret for gaining moksha: ask for the signs of those who went before, ask the lineages of the deceiving gurus, ask where they all perished together; in talk and in maya there is nothing, the babblers do not see the state; and when the noisy camp breaks up, the breath has gone with the whole of it.
2410.nuance: பாளையம் is an army camp; the body as a camp that breaks up at death is the verse's own image, and கூட்டோடே போச்சுது (went with the whole) is the breath leaving with the body. Whether ஏய்ச்சலது குருக்கள் means gurus who deceive or gurus who are mocked turns on ஏய்ச்சல், which tradition takes as deceit.

2411.reading: Where the breath subsided and went no one sees, nor the dwellings of moksha and hell, nor the ascent of the way by which it came, nor the jewelled way where the wind changes and stands; look well at the open space, for the Vedas and shastras have been emptied out; it is as if settled in the embryo, and only he knows it, so look with awareness.
2411.nuance: The verse says four times that no one sees (காணார்), and leaves open whether 'he who alone knows' is God or the knower. வளிமாறி நிற்குமணி வழி (the jewel way where the wind changes) is read by tradition as the central channel where the two breaths exchange. வெளியாய்ப் போச்சே is either 'have gone to the open', that is, been exposed as empty, or 'have become space'. வெட்டவெளி, the open space, is the Siddhars' term for the void of awareness.

2412.reading: Look: births in the world are crores, and creations of many kinds crores upon crores; births in the cosmos are crores; see how it dances in space; you are the one within the atom-space; the wonder is a worm's nest struck by a net; the cosmos becomes the body, and when one becomes of that nature it is truth.
2412.nuance: Lines 6 and 8 are damaged (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா, குணவியவா னானக்காற்), and the reading of them is a guess. The clear claim is அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும், the cosmos becomes the body: the macrocosm is in the microcosm, the Siddhars' அண்டபிண்டம். அணுவெளி (atom-space) places the self at once in the smallest point and in space.

2413.reading: If you are human you must have truth; do no base act and do not err; do not drop the daily rites, and do not shift from your state, leaving observance, firm practice and samadhi; do not wander witless, do not lie, do not forget merit, do not pick quarrels and dispute with raised voice, and do not walk about as a ritualist: the ray is complete.
2413.nuance: The verse keeps the daily rites (நித்தியகர்மம் விடாதே) yet forbids walking as a கர்மி, a ritualist; the distinction is between doing one's duties and making ritual one's identity. The syntax of lines 3 and 4 allows 'do not leave observance, firm practice and samadhi' or 'having left them, do not shift from the state'; the first fits the list of prohibitions. கதிர்தான் முற்றே (the ray is complete) closes the run.

links.note: Both make release a matter of the mind knowing with certainty: the Kural's mind that ponders and knows what is need not think of birth again; Agasthiyar's mind subdued by devotion, knowing the state in the whorl, has moksha itself. Agasthiyar adds the yogic place; the Kural does not.

Tirumular sets the learned, the ascetics and the virgins each in their own enclosure and says none knows the Lord's nature; Agasthiyar's Vedic men, each at variance with the other, wail in the streets and none sees the divine state. Both make sectarian learning a sign of not knowing.

Konganar's man who does not know the standing of pooranam lies, recites crores of mantras and, a mere 'effect guru', robs his disciples; Agasthiyar's crores of thieves beguile with words. The same figure, the teacher as thief, in two works.

Tirumular says people do not know the great Being that swallows body and awareness; Agasthiyar says no one sees where the breath went or the way it came, and only 'he' knows. Both locate the unknowable at the point where body and life part, and both tell the reader to look with awareness rather than scripture.

Tirumular sees the holy form of the cosmos standing like milk in water within the vessel of the body; Agasthiyar says the cosmos becomes the body (அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும்). The image of the macrocosm held in the microcosm is shared; Tirumular's is an experience of bliss, Agasthiyar's a doctrine stated.

Pattinathar addresses pooranam as having taken a form that makes the whole cosmos-and-body (அண்டபிண்டம்) atom within atom; Agasthiyar places the self in the atom-space and says the cosmos becomes the body. Both use the Siddhars' compound for the cosmos mirrored in the body.

The Kural sets truth spoken with the heart above austerity and giving; Agasthiyar makes truth the first requirement of being human and closes the run on it, while keeping rites and samadhi in their place below it.

new_concepts.gloss: the cosmos (அண்டம்) and the body (பிண்டம்) as one: the Siddhars' doctrine that what is in the universe is in the body, so that the body is the field of knowledge and practice
new_concepts.label_source: 2412 says அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும், the cosmos becomes the body; the compound அண்டபிண்டம் is used elsewhere in the corpus (Pattinathar, Pambatti, Valmiki).

source_issues: 2407 line 3: ஒன்றொன்றுக்கு கொன்றை மாறி is corrupt; the sense requires ஒன்றுக்கொன்று மாறி (each at variance with the other).
2412 line 6 (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா) and line 8 (குணவியவா னானக்காற்) are garbled and cannot be construed with confidence.
2411 and 2413 end with a semicolon rather than the stanza's usual close; the final line of 2413 (கதிர்தான் முற்றே) marks the end of the run, so the run is complete as printed.
